titleDv: ޤާނޫނު ނަންބަރު 11/2022 (ހެއްކާބެހޭ ޤާނޫނު) އަށް ... ވަނަ އިޞްލާޙު ގެނައުމުގެ ބިލު
summary: This government bill, presented by the Bilehdhoo MP, amends the Evidence Act (Law No. 11/2022), the law on what evidence courts can accept and how. It rewrites the rules on hearsay, copies of documents, electronic evidence, demonstrations and site inspections, and witnesses who refresh their memory from earlier statements. It adds two new chapters: one on character evidence, including limits on raising a victim's sexual history in sexual offence cases, and one on identification evidence. It also rewrites Article 136 on when a court can order a journalist to reveal a source, and repeals Articles 51, 59, 75 and 91. The scanned pages for the identification chapter and the new Article 136 are hard to read, so some details there come from the comparison table at the end of the bill.
whyItMatters: These rules decide what a judge can rely on in criminal and civil trials, from WhatsApp records to an absent witness's statement. Journalists would only have to reveal sources in a narrower set of serious crimes, and only through the High Court.
keyProvisions: Articles 57 to 59: the split between 'first-degree' and 'second-degree' documentary evidence is dropped. A document can be proved by the original or by listed alternatives such as a certified copy, a business record or a printout from stored data, and secondary proof is allowed when the original is lost, destroyed in good faith or held by someone else.

Article 67: courts must presume the device that recorded or stored electronic evidence was working properly, unless the side challenging it proves a fault that affected the evidence. Courts weigh the evidence's nature, purpose and how it was recorded.

Articles 117 to 119-1: hearsay can be admitted only if the circumstances make it reliable and the speaker cannot attend court. New grounds include a witness who needs protection the court cannot give, and a witness who cannot be found despite reasonable efforts.

New Articles 129-1 to 129-6 (character evidence): evidence of a person's character cannot be used to show they acted in line with it, with exceptions for an accused person's good character. In sexual offence cases, the victim's sexual history or reputation generally cannot be used, with narrow exceptions and a notice procedure.

New Articles 129-7 to 129-10 add a chapter on identification evidence, meaning evidence that a witness identified a suspect, and set rules for accepting it. Most of this part of the scan is unreadable.

Article 136: a journalist's source can be ordered revealed only when needed to identify or stop a suspect in organised crime (Law 32/2015, Law 10/2014) or listed national security offences under the Penal Code. The Prosecutor General, suspect or accused applies to the High Court, which must hear the journalist, decide within 24 hours and weigh the public interest. Appeals go to the Supreme Court within 10 days, and 'journalist' includes freelancers.
whoIsAffected: Judges, prosecutors, lawyers, police investigators, witnesses and victims in court cases, and journalists and their sources.
statedReasons: The government says the Evidence Act causes difficulties in criminal and civil cases and needs added rules and procedures. It also says Article 136, on forcing journalists to reveal sources, has raised concerns among journalists that this bill addresses.
